Kreplach

Served at: Yom Kippur (Day of Atonement)

Serves 6Prep 45 minCook 30 min

Kreplach are traditional Jewish dumplings filled with meat or other fillings, commonly served on Yom Kippur, particularly at the break-fast meal. They symbolize hidden blessings and are enjoyed in soups or fried as a comforting dish after the day of fasting.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups all-purpose flour (240 g)
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/3 cup water (80 ml), plus more if needed
  • 1 tablespoon vegetable oil
  • 1/2 pound ground beef (225 g)
  • 1 small onion, finely chopped
  • 1 clove garlic, minced
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
  • 1/4 teaspoon paprika
  • 2 tablespoons vegetable oil for frying (optional)
  • 6 cups chicken or beef broth (1.4 L) for serving

Method

  1. In a bowl, combine flour and salt.
  2. Make a well in the center and add eggs, water, and 1 tablespoon vegetable oil.
  3. Mix and knead until a smooth dough forms, adding more water if needed.
  4. Cover dough and let rest for 30 minutes.
  5. Meanwhile, prepare the filling by sautéing onion and garlic in a little oil until translucent.
  6. Add ground beef, salt, pepper, and paprika; cook until meat is browned and cooked through. Let cool.
  7. Roll out the dough thinly on a floured surface.
  8. Cut into 3-inch (7.5 cm) squares.
  9. Place about 1 teaspoon of filling in the center of each square.
  10. Fold the dough over to form a triangle and press edges firmly to seal.
  11. Bring broth to a simmer in a large pot.
  12. Add kreplach in batches and cook for 8-10 minutes until they float to the surface and are tender.
  13. Serve kreplach in hot broth or drain and fry in vegetable oil until golden for a crispy variation.

Tips

  • For a vegetarian version, substitute the meat filling with mashed potatoes or sautéed mushrooms.
  • Ensure the dough is rolled thinly for delicate kreplach that cook evenly.
  • Kreplach can be made ahead and frozen before cooking; cook from frozen by adding a few extra minutes to the boiling time.
